title: Connect to Notion MCP
snippet:
The easiest way to connect is through your AI assistant’s connector or plugin library. You can also browse available connections in Notion under **Settings** → **Notion MCP**.

## Manual setup
Add Notion MCP using a server URL or client configuration.
##
​
Connect from your AI assistant
Open your AI assistant’s connector or plugin library and search for **Notion**. Select it and follow the prompts to authorize access to your Notion workspace. After you authorize the connection, your AI assistant can read and update content that you can access in the selected workspace. If Notion isn’t listed, check whether your assistant supports adding a custom MCP server and follow manual setup.
##
​
Connect from Notion
In Notion, open **Settings** → **Notion MCP** and browse the directory. Select your AI assistant and follow its connection instructions.
##
​
Manual setup
Use these instructions if you’re adding Notion as a custom MCP server or configuring a client directly. The remote server URL is `https://mcp.notion.com/mcp`.

If your MCP client isn’t listed above, add Notion as a remote MCP server:
- **Streamable HTTP (recommended):** `https://mcp.notion.com/mcp`
- **SSE fallback:** `https://mcp.notion.com/sse` — use this only if the client doesn’t support Streamable HTTP.

Some MCP clients only support local stdio servers. You can still connect to Notion MCP using the [mcp-remote](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote) bridge:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"notion": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.notion.com/mcp"]
}
}
}
```
As a last resort, you can run our [open-source MCP server](https://github.com/makenotion/notion-mcp-server) locally, though this package is no longer actively maintained.
- Complete the OAuth flow when prompted.
- Disconnect and reconnect the client. Look for **Clear authentication** or **Disconnect** in its MCP settings.
- Check your permissions in the Notion workspace that you’re trying to access.

**Notion MCP** (`https://mcp.notion.com/mcp`) is our hosted, actively maintained server. It supports OAuth authorization and MCP tokens, and requires no infrastructure setup.The **open-source server** ([`notion-mcp-server`](https://github.com/makenotion/notion-mcp-server)) is no longer actively maintained. It authenticates with an integration token and requires you to manage your own connection and deployment.For most users, we recommend Notion MCP.

title: Build an MCP client for Notion
Notion MCP
snippet:
Notion MCP lets an [MCP client](/guides/mcp/common-mcp-clients), such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex, connect to your Notion workspace through the [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction).
##
​
How Notion MCP works
Notion MCP is a remote MCP server hosted by Notion. After you authorize a connection with OAuth, the MCP client can use Notion MCP tools to read and update content that you can access.

What you can do
MCP clients can combine Notion MCP tools to:
- Search content in Notion and connected sources.
- Read, create, and update Notion content.
- Create pages and databases.
See [Supported tools](/guides/mcp/mcp-supported-tools) for the current tool list, or [connect an MCP client](/guides/mcp/get-started-with-mcp).
##
​
Admin controls
Workspace owners can manage MCP client access in **Settings** → **Notion MCP** → **Manage workspace clients**. Limiting which clients members can connect needs the Enterprise plan. Organization owners can also use the Admin API to [list](/reference/admin/list-mcp-client-connections) and [revoke](/reference/admin/revoke-mcp-client-connection) members’ connections. See [Admin controls for MCP](https://www.notion.com/help/notion-mcp#admin-controls-for-mcp) in the Notion Help Center for workspace settings and allowlists.
